rounds.hypothesis: Per diagnose.json, two independent absent guards on the epoll_ctl entry path. (1) EPERM: Asterinas has no equivalent of Linux's file_can_poll, because Pollable::poll is a required trait method on FileLike, so every file is pollable by construction and there is no null f_op->poll to test; the invariant is that pollability is a property of the file description's *type*, not of the inode type, so the predicate has to live on the file description or regular files, /dev/null and procfs text files stay wrongly acceptable. (2) EINVAL: no self-add rejection exists, and the comparison must be on file-description identity rather than the fd number so that dup(epfd) is caught too. The companion constraint that bounds the fix: a non-pollable file must still report itself unconditionally ready to poll/select, so Pollable::poll must not be touched.
rounds.change: Added `supports_event_polling()` to `FileLike` (kernel/src/fs/file/file_handle.rs), defaulting to true, and mirrored it on `PerOpenFileOps` (kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs). `InodeHandle` overrides it to `self.open_file.as_ref().is_some_and(|f| f.supports_event_polling())`, i.e. false exactly when `poll` falls through to the unconditional IN|OUT mask -- which is the regular-file and directory case across every filesystem. Overrode it to false on the nine `PerOpenFileOps` implementors whose `poll` returns a constant mask (MemFile except /dev/random, HwRngFile, TdxGuestFile, FbHandle, OpenBlockFile, MapsFileHandle, MemFileHandle, VirtioFsDir, NsFile) and on the two `FileLike` implementors with an empty-mask poll (FsConfigFile, DetachedMountFile), each with a reference to the matching Linux fops table showing no `.poll` hook. Enforced both rules once at the top of `EpollFile::control` (kernel/src/events/epoll/file.rs), before the Add/Del/Mod dispatch so all three ops are covered: EPERM when `!file.supports_event_polling()`, then EINVAL when the resolved target downcasts to `EpollFile` and `core::ptr::eq` says it is this same epoll file. Left `Pollable::poll` untouched everywhere. Uncommented epoll_ctl02 in all.txt.
rounds.outcome: green on the first round: `All conformance tests passed.`, make exit 0, 9 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped, matching the host's 9/0/0 exactly. Both previously-failing subtests now pass (EPERM on the O_DIRECTORY fd, EINVAL on fd == epfd). Verified in the same boot that the other 16 enabled epoll tests still pass (340 passed / 0 failed across 17 tests), and separately that `make check` is clean and the full `AUTO_TEST=regression` suite is green.

layer: Both invariants were patched at the layers diagnose.json's owning_layer named, at its two different seams. (1) EPERM: the capability predicate is declared on `FileLike` (the per-open file description layer) and answered concretely by `InodeHandle`, which is the object that owns the always-ready fallback; the ~30 `Inode::open` implementors and the 14 `PerOpenFileOps` implementors get one place to opt out, and no check was pushed down into ext2/exfat/ramfs. (2) EINVAL: the identity comparison is at the top of `EpollFile::control`, which diagnose named as the equivalent of the syscall entry layer. I chose `control` over `sys_epoll_ctl` for both checks because it already resolves the target file (file.rs:72-74) and holds `&self` for the epoll file, so neither check resolves an fd twice, and both apply to Add/Del/Mod from one site -- diagnose explicitly offered this as the alternative placement and flagged that doing it in `add_interest` alone would be wrong.
generalizes:
The predicate is a property of the file description, so it is correct for inputs and callers this test never supplies. Measured on the host with a purpose-built probe (/tmp/epoll_probe.c, scratch, not committed) covering 20+ file types, and the fix reproduces Linux's answer for every one -- including the ones LTP never samples: epoll_ctl on a regular file, /dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/full, /dev/urandom, /proc/self/maps, /proc/self/mem, /proc/self/ns/mnt, an fsopen() fd and a framebuffer all return EPERM on Linux and now do here, while a pipe end, socket, eventfd, timerfd, /dev/ptmx, /dev/random, /dev/kmsg and a *different* epoll file are all still accepted. There is no branch anywhere on the O_DIRECTORY flag, the directory inode type, the fd number, or the errno the test happens to use: epoll_ctl02 samples the rule with a directory, but the code never mentions directories, and a regular file -- which the test never tries -- is rejected by the same line.

Independently corroborated by two gvisor cases that assert exactly these invariants and were blocklisted before this change: `EpollTest.RegularFiles` (EPERM on a regular file) and `EpollTest.CycleOfOneDisallowed` (EINVAL on self-add) both pass now, having failed at base. They stay blocklisted since enabling them is out of scope for this run, but they are the strongest evidence this is not fitted to LTP's sampling. `EpollTest.CycleOfThreeDisallowed` still fails, and deliberately so: multi-level cycle detection (ELOOP via a nesting-depth walk) is a separate missing feature, it fails identically at base, and rejecting nested epoll files to make it pass would be wrong -- the host confirms adding a *different* epoll file must succeed.

The companion constraint diagnose raised is respected by construction: `Pollable::poll` is not modified anywhere in the patch, so poll/select/ppoll still report regular files and directories as POLLIN|POLLOUT (host revents=0x5). That is why the fix adds a separate predicate instead of weakening the existing mask -- the mask is read by every poll/select/epoll_wait caller in the kernel. Verified no regression: the 16 other enabled epoll tests plus poll01/03/04, ppoll01, pselect02/03, select01/03 and the read/write/open/pipe/stat/mmap/dup/fcntl/lseek/getdents group all pass (210 passed, and the only 6 failures in that selector run -- getdents02, ioctl01, ioctl02 -- are testcases still commented out in all.txt that I confirmed fail identically at base by stashing the kernel diff), and the whole `AUTO_TEST=regression` suite is green.

On per-file overrides I deliberately followed Linux's fops tables rather than guessing, so the change never rejects something Linux accepts: /dev/random keeps event polling (Linux's `random_fops` has `.poll`; it blocks for entropy) while /dev/urandom loses it, and `VirtioFsFile` was left at the default `true` because `fuse_file_operations` *does* install `.poll` -- only `fuse_dir_operations` does not, so just the directory handle was overridden.
fix_summary:
Gives the file-description layer an explicit `supports_event_polling()` capability query and has epoll_ctl enforce it, plus a file-description identity check rejecting an epoll file monitoring itself.

Designed against Asterinas's `FileLike`/`PerOpenFileOps` traits rather than transplanting Linux's structure, because the two do not line up here and that mismatch is the actual root cause. Linux gets this rule for free: `f_op->poll` is a nullable function pointer, so `file_can_poll` is literally `return file->f_op->poll;` and `vfs_poll` substitutes `DEFAULT_POLLMASK` when it is NULL -- one nullable field encodes both "has an event source" and "is always ready". In Asterinas `Pollable::poll` is a *required* trait method, so there is no null state to test and every file is pollable by construction. The Asterinas-shaped expression of that missing distinction is a defaulted predicate on the file description, sitting beside `settable_status_flags` and `access_mode` -- the other per-file-description capability queries -- and answered for inode-backed files by `InodeHandle` delegating to its optional per-open file object. That delegation is what makes it a fix rather than a special case: `open_file.is_none()` is exactly the condition under which `poll` returns the unconditional IN|OUT mask, so "has no per-open object" and "is unconditionally ready" are the same fact, read from the one place that knows it, instead of an `InodeType::Dir` test inside the epoll code.

The self-add check uses `core::ptr::eq` on the downcast target against `self`, mirroring Linux's `f.file == tf.file` pointer comparison rather than an fd comparison; since `dup` clones the `Arc<dyn FileLike>` (FileTable::duplicate_entry) rather than the file, this catches `dup(epfd)` as Linux does, and leaves nesting a different epoll instance working. Both checks sit before the Add/Del/Mod dispatch in `EpollFile::control`, in Linux's order (EBADF on both fds, then EPERM, then the EINVAL identity check), which the host probe confirms matters: a non-pollable target reports EPERM even when the op is also invalid.

One divergence worth naming: Linux resolves errnos in `do_epoll_ctl` after its syscall wrapper has already copied the user event, so EFAULT precedes EPERM. Asterinas reads the event in `sys_epoll_ctl` before resolving epfd, which is the same relative position, so that ordering already matched and needed no change -- confirmed by the EFAULT and invalid-op subtests, which passed before and after.
